video:video.video:title: The King of Aksum Who Changed Gods on His Coins
video:video.video:description: Ezana of Aksum put the cross on his gold coins where the crescent had been. When and why? His stones, an emperor's letter and a scholars' dispute.

video:video.video:title: Battle of Adwa: The Treaty Line That Meant Two Things
video:video.video:description: Battle of Adwa, 1896: one treaty article, two texts. Italian 'consents', Amharic 'it shall be possible'. Trick or slip? Then Rome's telegram and a night march.

video:video.video:title: Ain Jalut, 1260: Slave Soldiers Against the Mongols
video:video.video:description: Who won the Battle of Ain Jalut in 1260, and how? Slave soldiers, a captured Mongol general's last words, four sizes for one army, two endings, one myth.

video:video.video:title: Cannae, 216 BC: The Gold Rings Hannibal Sent to Carthage
video:video.video:description: How many Romans died at Cannae in 216 BC? Polybius and Livy compared: the trap, two deaths for Paullus, the gold rings sent to Carthage, a debated site.

video:video.video:title: Warship Rams Found Where Rome Won the First Punic War
video:video.video:description: What happened at the Battle of the Egadi Islands, 241 B.C.? A fleet paid for by citizens, 27 rams on the seabed, and a puzzle: most readable rams are Roman.

video:video.video:title: Hattin, 1187: The Battle That Lost the True Cross
video:video.video:description: Why did the crusaders lose the Battle of Hattin in 1187? One small spring, a midnight council, the True Cross taken, and Saladin's words: until that tent falls.

video:video.video:title: Ramesses II Said He Won the Battle of Kadesh Alone
video:video.video:description: Did Ramesses II win the Battle of Kadesh, about 1274 B.C.? Two Bedouin who lied, beaten scouts, the rescuers on his own walls and the Hittite verdict.

video:video.video:title: Mongol Invasion of Japan: What Sank Kublai Khan's Fleet?
video:video.video:description: What sank Kublai Khan's fleet in the Mongol invasion of Japan? The kamikaze, a wall at Hakata Bay, a bomb painted in later? And the wrecks off Takashima.

video:video.video:title: Salamis, 480 BC: Xerxes' Scribes Took Names
video:video.video:description: What happened at the Battle of Salamis, 480 B.C.? Xerxes watched as scribes took names, Artemisia's ram, the beheaded Phoenicians: three records that disagree.

video:video.video:title: Teutoburg Forest, AD 9: What Kalkriese Found
video:video.video:description: Where was the Battle of the Teutoburg Forest? The finds at Kalkriese: a mule still wearing its bell, a stripped silver mask, bone pits, and the case against.

video:video.video:title: How Chess Began, and Why the Queen Got Her Power
video:video.video:description: Where did chess come from? India, Persia and Baghdad, the earliest known pieces, and the 1400s change that made the queen the strongest piece.

video:video.video:title: Hadrian's Wall: Turf, Stone and Milecastles
video:video.video:description: Who built Hadrian's Wall, and what was it for? Milecastles, the Turf Wall, the Vallum, Roman obstacle pits, and a souvenir pan that may hold its Roman name.

video:video.video:title: Knight's Armour: From Mail to Plate
video:video.video:description: How did knight armour go from mail to plate? The Visby graves of 1361, how heavy armour was, a helmet worth a cow, the crane myth and a treadmill test.

video:video.video:title: The Bayeux Tapestry: What It Really Shows
video:video.video:description: What does the Bayeux Tapestry really show? Harold's arrow in the eye, likely added in the 1800s, the oath at Bayeux, the lost end, checked against the sources.

video:video.video:title: How a Medieval Castle Was Built: "The Greatest Castle Never Built"
video:video.video:description: How was a medieval castle built? Beaumaris, 1296: a letter asking for 400 masons and £250 a week, spiral scaffolding, and who designed Edward I's castles.

video:video.video:title: The Dardanelles Gun: The Giant Bombard That Unscrews in Two
video:video.video:description: What is the Dardanelles Gun? A 17-tonne bronze bombard cast in 1464 for Mehmed II that unscrews in two, and what it tells us about the guns of 1453.

video:video.video:title: Domesday Book: Why Was It Made?
video:video.video:description: Why was Domesday Book made? William the Conqueror's survey of 1086: the questions asked, one entry decoded, the missing animals and the historians' answers.

video:video.video:title: Krak des Chevaliers: The Best-Preserved Crusader Castle
video:video.video:description: How did Krak des Chevaliers fall? The crusader castle UNESCO ranks among the best preserved, Baybars' siege of 1271, and a letter two chronicles call a fake.

video:video.video:title: The Lewis Chessmen: Why the Warders Bite Their Shields
video:video.video:description: Why do four Lewis chessmen bite their shields? 93 ivory pieces found on Lewis in 1831, Norway or Iceland, berserkers or a joke, and the £5 warder of 2019.

video:video.video:title: 172 Longbows from the Mary Rose: The Largest Collection Found
video:video.video:description: How hard was an English longbow to draw? The 172 yew bows of the Mary Rose, sunk in 1545: their length, the draw weight dispute and the archer's bones.

video:video.video:title: The Trebuchet: How It Really Worked
video:video.video:description: How did a trebuchet work? Rope crews, then a falling weight: the Warwolf at Stirling in 1304, the stone that killed Simon de Montfort, a 168 m replica shot.

video:video.video:title: The Mystery of the Antikythera Mechanism
video:video.video:description: What was the Antikythera mechanism? A Greek gear box found in a shipwreck in 1900. Who made it, and why do the holes under its calendar ring divide scholars?

video:video.video:title: Tanzwut: The Dancing Plague of 1518
video:video.video:description: What was the dancing plague of 1518? Strasbourg's council papers, four chronicles and Paracelsus: the dancers' names, the cure, and did anyone really die?

video:video.video:title: Easter Island's Heads Have Bodies
video:video.video:description: Easter Island's heads have bodies. How did the Rapa Nui move moai of many tonnes, and why did the carving stop? Ship logs, a 2012 walk and the dispute.

video:video.video:title: The Mystery of Rome's Lost Legion
video:video.video:description: What happened to Rome's lost Ninth Legion? Its last dated stone at York, its tiles at Nijmegen, Tacitus, Fronto and Dio, and the latest research.

video:video.video:title: Who Were the Sea Peoples?
video:video.video:description: Who were the Sea Peoples, and did they cause the Bronze Age collapse? Egypt's reliefs, Ugarit's last letters, tree rings and Philistine DNA weigh the evidence.

video:video.video:title: The Mystery of Stonehenge's Altar Stone
video:video.video:description: Stonehenge's Altar Stone was traced to Scotland in 2024; in 2026 no outcrop examined matched. Where is it from, how did six tonnes travel, and why?

video:video.video:title: The Mystery of the Voynich Manuscript
video:video.video:description: What is the Voynich manuscript, who made it, and has anyone decoded it? Carbon dating, letters from Prague and Rome, and the claims that failed.

video:video.video:title: What Is a Caltrop?
video:video.video:description: What is a caltrop? A Roman four-spiked iron: the name tribulus, Gaugamela, Vegetius' chariots, Scipio's refusal, finds at Caerleon and Enns, and three myths.

video:video.video:title: The Roman Fort: 752 Men, No Beer, One Birthday
video:video.video:description: What was inside a Roman fort? Vindolanda's layered forts, the textbook plan, a strength report of 752 men, a beer request and a birthday letter, all sourced.

video:video.video:title: What Was the Gladius, Really? Rome's Sword
video:video.video:description: What was the Roman gladius? The Spanish sword in Polybius and the Suda, a real dispute over its origin, the Mainz and Pompeii types, and the Sword of Tiberius.

video:video.video:title: Roman Helmets: From Montefortino to Imperial Gallic
video:video.video:description: What did Roman soldiers wear on their heads? Montefortino, Coolus and Imperial Gallic helmets, why none of these names is Roman, and the finds that show it.

video:video.video:title: The Roman Onager: Rome's One-Armed Stone-Thrower
video:video.video:description: The Roman onager, a one-armed stone-thrower named after a wild ass: how it worked, Amida in A.D. 359, Vegetius' ten per legion, and what no source tells us.

video:video.video:title: The Roman Pilum: Why the Javelin Bent
video:video.video:description: Was the Roman pilum designed to bend? What Polybius, Caesar and Plutarch say, the metal of early pila, modern throwing tests and 22 bent points in a Roman well.

video:video.video:title: What Was a Pugio?
video:video.video:description: What was a pugio? Rome's dagger: the coin of Caesar's killers, the Scaevinus and Arria stories, the 2019 Haltern find, and a real dispute over its origin.

video:video.video:title: The Roman Scorpion: Rome's Sniper Weapon
video:video.video:description: A Gaulish warrior on a burning wall is hit by a bolt from a machine he never saw. The Roman scorpion was a torsion bolt-shooter powered by twisted sinew and...

video:video.video:title: The Roman Shield
video:video.video:description: What was the Roman scutum made of? Polybius's bull-hide glue, the Dura-Europos shield's 5 mm of glued wood strips, and the dispute over how heavy it was.

video:video.video:title: Lorica Segmentata: The Armour from Corbridge
video:video.video:description: What was the lorica segmentata? The 1964 Corbridge chest, the 2018 Kalkriese cuirass, why the name isn't Roman, and what Trajan's Column really shows.

video:video.video:title: Roman Bullets: Insults Cast in Lead
video:video.video:description: What were Roman lead sling bullets? Inscribed glandes from the siege of Perusia, a forger who fooled himself, and Burnswark: siege or firing range?

video:video.video:title: 10 Famous Battles, Ranked by What They Changed
video:video.video:description: Ten famous battles, Kadesh to Adwa, ranked by what they changed. Why does Cannae come last, which battle comes first, and how well do we know each?
